paragraphs.en: The US$3-million Fundamental Physics Prize is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year’s award in March. And it is far from the only one of its type. As a News Feature article in Nature discusses, a string of lucrative awards for researchers have joined the Nobel Prizes in recent years. Many, like the Fundamental Physics Prize, are funded from the telephone-number-sized bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs.These benefactors have succeeded in their chosen fields, they say, and they want to use their wealth to draw attention to those who have succeeded in science.
paragraphs.zh: 正如亚历山大·波利亚科夫今年三月领奖时所说，奖金高达三百万美元的基础物理学奖，确实是一项有趣的实验。而它远非同类奖项中唯一的一个。正如《自然》的一篇新闻特写所讨论的，近年来，一连串面向研究人员、奖金丰厚的奖项加入了诺贝尔奖的行列。其中许多奖项与基础物理学奖一样，资金来自互联网企业家那些余额位数堪比电话号码的银行账户。这些资助者说，他们在自己选择的领域取得了成功，因此希望用财富让人们关注那些在科学上取得成功的人。

paragraphs.en: What’s not to like? Quite a lot, according to a handful of scientists quoted in the News Feature. You cannot buy class, as the old saying goes, and these upstart entrepreneurs cannot buy their prizes the prestige of the Nobels. The new awards are an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them, say scientists. They could distort the achievement-based system of peer-review-led research. They could cement the status quo of peer-reviewed research. They do not fund peer-reviewed research. They perpetuate the myth of the lone genius.
paragraphs.zh: 这有什么不好呢？按照新闻特写中引用的少数科学家的说法，问题可不少。俗话说，金钱买不来品位，这些新近发迹的企业家也无法为自己的奖项买来诺贝尔奖的声望。科学家们说，这些新奖项不过是幕后出资者的一场自我宣传。它们可能扭曲由同行评审主导、以成就为依据的科研体系；可能使经过同行评审的研究现状更加固化；它们并不资助经过同行评审的科研项目；还会延续孤独天才的神话。

paragraphs.en: The goals of the prize-givers seem as scattered as the criticism. Some want to shock, others to draw people into science, or to better reward those who have made their careers in research.
paragraphs.zh: 颁奖者的目标似乎和这些批评一样五花八门。有些人想造成轰动，有些人想吸引人们投身科学，还有些人想更好地奖励那些以研究为终身事业的人。

paragraphs.en: As Nature has pointed out before, there are some legitimate concerns about how science prizes – both new and old – are distributed. The Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, launched this year, takes an unrepresentative view of what the life sciences include. But the Nobel Foundation’s limit of three recipients per prize, each of whom must still be living, has long been outgrown by the collaborative nature of modern research – as will be demonstrated by the inevitable row over who is ignored when it comes to acknowledging the discovery of the Higgs boson. The Nobels were, of course, themselves set up by a very rich individual who had decided what he wanted to do with his own money. Time, rather than intention, has given them legitimacy.
paragraphs.zh: 正如《自然》此前所指出的，对于新旧科学奖项的分配方式，确实存在一些合理的担忧。今年设立的生命科学突破奖，对生命科学所涵盖内容的认识并不具有代表性。但诺贝尔基金会规定，每个奖项最多只能授予三人，而且获奖者都必须健在，这一限制早已不适应现代研究的合作性质：在表彰希格斯玻色子的发现时，围绕哪些人被忽略而必然引发的争论，就将证明这一点。当然，诺贝尔奖本身也是由一位极其富有的个人设立的，他自行决定了如何使用自己的钱。赋予这些奖项公信力的是时间，而不是设立者的初衷。

paragraphs.en: As much as some scientists may complain about the new awards, two things seem clear. First, most researchers would accept such a prize if they were offered one. Second, it is surely a good thing that the money and attention come to science rather than go elsewhere. It is fair to criticize and question the mechanism– that is the culture of research, after all – but it is the prize-givers’ money to do with as they please. It is wise to take such gifts with gratitude and grace.
paragraphs.zh: 无论一些科学家如何抱怨这些新奖项，有两点似乎是明确的。第一，如果获得这样的奖项，大多数研究人员都会接受。第二，资金和关注流向科学而不是其他地方，无疑是一件好事。批评和质疑评奖机制完全合理，毕竟这就是研究文化；但那是颁奖者自己的钱，他们有权按自己的意愿使用。心怀感激、从容得体地接受这样的馈赠，才是明智之举。
